title.en: Volume 337 Biographies 124: Lu Chao, Tu Er Bing A, A Si Ha, Gong Zhaolin, Yang Jingsu, Min Eyuan
title.raw: 卷337 列傳一百二十四 卢焯 图尔炳阿 阿思哈 宫兆麟 杨景素 闵鹗元

sentences.zh: 列傳一百二十四

translations.literal: Biography 124
translations.idiomatic: Biography 124

sentences.zh: 盧焯圖爾炳阿阿思哈宮兆麟楊景素閔鶚元

translations.literal: Lu Chao, Tu Erbinga, Asiha, Gong Zhaolin, Yang Jingsu, and Min Eyuan
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chao, Tu Erbinga, Asiha, Gong Zhaolin, Yang Jingsu, and Min Eyuan

sentences.zh: 盧焯，字光植，漢軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Lu Chao, style name Guangzhi, was a Chinese Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chao, whose style was Guangzhi, belonged to the Chinese Banner corps of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 入貲授直隸武邑知縣。

translations.literal: He purchased office and was appointed magistrate of Wuyi in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: By purchasing office he received appointment as magistrate of Wuyi in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 縣舊有均徭錢供差費，遇差仍按裡派夫，焯革除之，又歸火耗於公，捕盜尤力。

translations.literal: The county had long levied equitable labor-service money for dispatch expenses, yet when corvée was due still assigned laborers by li; Chao abolished this, also returned surcharge grain to the public treasury, and was especially vigorous in apprehending bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The county had long collected equitable corvée funds for official errands, yet whenever labor was requisitioned it still drafted men by neighborhood; Chao abolished the practice, restored surcharge grain to the public account, and pursued bandits with particular energy.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，解餉詣京師，世宗特召對。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, while escorting funds to the capital, he was specially summoned for audience by the Yongzheng Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongzheng [1728], he delivered tax silver to the capital and was granted a special audience by Emperor Yongzheng.

sentences.zh: 遷江南亳州知州，禁械鬥。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Bozhou in Jiangnan and prohibited armed brawls.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Bozhou in Jiangnan, where he suppressed armed faction fights.

sentences.zh: 再遷山東東昌知府，總督田文鏡遣官弁四出訪事，東昌民逮下獄甚眾，焯至，悉判遣之。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to be prefect of Dongchang in Shandong. Governor Tian Wenjing had sent officials in all directions to investigate matters; many Dongchang commoners had been arrested and imprisoned. When Chao arrived, he judged and released them all.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to serve as prefect of Dongchang in Shandong. Governor Tian Wenjing had dispatched officers in every direction to investigate affairs, and a great many Dongchang residents had been thrown into prison; when Chao took office he reviewed the cases and sent them all home.

sentences.zh: 會有水災，焯疏運河，築護城長堤，動帑賑恤。

translations.literal: When flood struck, Chao dredged the Grand Canal, built a long protective embankment around the city wall, and drew on the treasury for relief.
translations.idiomatic: A flood followed; Chao dredged the Grand Canal, raised a long protective dike around the city walls, and opened the treasury for relief.

sentences.zh: 上遣大臣閱視，獨東昌得完。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a minister to inspect; Dongchang alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: The throne dispatched a minister to inspect the damage, and Dongchang alone emerged intact.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷督糧道，移河南南汝道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Grain Transport Intendant, then moved to the Henan Nanru Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year [1731] he became Grain Transport Intendant, then was shifted to the Nanru Circuit in Henan.

sentences.zh: 十年，授按察使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year [1732] he received appointment as provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year [1733] he was promoted to provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢福建巡撫，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to governor of Fujian and granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year [1734] he was elevated to governor of Fujian and awarded a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 十三年，高宗即位，焯疏言被水州縣不成災，上諭曰：「被水雖不成災，仍須加意賑恤，毋使小民失所。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the Gaozong Emperor acceded, Chao memorialized that flooded prefectures and counties had not reached disaster level. The emperor instructed: "Though the flooding has not become a disaster, you must still give extra care to relief so that the common people do not lose their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year [1735], when Emperor Qianlong took the throne, Chao reported that flood-hit districts had not yet qualified as full disasters. The emperor replied: "Even if the waters have not risen to disaster level, you must still relieve the people with special care and keep the poor from losing their homes.

sentences.zh: 」乾隆元年，請查丈建陽民田，上諭曰：「小民畏查丈如水火。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Qianlong he requested a survey of civilian fields in Jianyang. The emperor instructed: "The common people dread land surveys as they dread fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: " In Qianlong 1 [1736] he asked to remeasure civilian fields in Jianyang. The throne answered: "Common people fear land surveys as they fear fire and flood.

sentences.zh: 汝初為加賦起見，今又以豁除掩非，一存觀望之心，所謂無一而可也。

translations.literal: You first acted with a view to increasing the tax levy; now you use exemption to cover wrongdoing, yet still keep a wait-and-see heart—there is not one thing that can be approved.
translations.idiomatic: You began with an eye to raising assessments; now you cloak your errors in exemptions while still holding back—nothing here is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 」尋奏減邵武永安所、霞浦福寧衛屯田徵米科則，豁閩、侯官諸縣額缺田地。

translations.literal: " Shortly thereafter he memorialized to reduce the grain-tax rates on garrison fields at Yongan Station in Shaowu and at Funing Guard in Xiapu, and to remit shortfall lands in Min, Houguan, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: " He soon memorialized to lower grain quotas on Yongan garrison fields in Shaowu and on Funing Guard fields in Xiapu, and to write off registered shortfall lands in Min, Houguan, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 又以平和、永安、清流諸縣田少丁多，請減免攤餘丁銀。

translations.literal: He also, because Pinghe, Yongan, Qingliu, and other counties had little land but many registered males, requested reduction or exemption of the apportioned surplus male tax silver.
translations.idiomatic: Because Pinghe, Yongan, Qingliu, and other counties had little land but many registered males, he also asked to reduce or exempt the apportioned surplus male tax.

sentences.zh: 又奏教民蠶績，疏濬省會城河。

translations.literal: He further memorialized to teach the people sericulture and to dredge the provincial capital city moat.
translations.idiomatic: He further urged instruction in sericulture among the people and dredging of the provincial capital moat.

sentences.zh: 三年，調浙江巡撫，兼鹽政。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to governor of Zhejiang, concurrently supervising the salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year [1738] he was transferred to governor of Zhejiang with concurrent charge of the salt administration.

sentences.zh: 奏請停仁和、海寧二縣草塘歲修銀，減嘉興屬七縣銀米十之二。

translations.literal: He memorialized to halt the annual repair silver for grass embankments in Renhe and Haining counties and to reduce grain and silver levies in the seven counties under Jiaxing by two-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to stop annual repair funds for grass revetments in Renhe and Haining and to cut grain and silver levies in the seven counties subordinate to Jiaxing by twenty percent.

sentences.zh: 又奏陳鹽政諸事：請禁商人短秤；

translations.literal: He also memorialized on various salt matters: requesting prohibition of merchants using short weights;
translations.idiomatic: He also laid out salt reforms: merchants were not to use short weights;

sentences.zh: 飭州縣捕私鹽毋擾民；

translations.literal: ordering prefectures and counties to seize smuggled salt without harassing the people;
translations.idiomatic: prefectures and counties were to seize contraband salt without troubling ordinary people;

sentences.zh: 毋捕肩挑小販；

translations.literal: not to arrest peddlers carrying salt on shoulder poles;
translations.idiomatic: porters selling salt by the load were not to be arrested;

sentences.zh: 鹽場徵課不得刑比。

translations.literal: and that salt-field tax collection must not use corporal punishment for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: and salt-field tax collection must not rely on torture to extract payment.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「所奏各條皆是。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "Each item you memorialized is correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Every point in your memorial is sound.

sentences.zh: 汝先過刻，茲乃事事以寬沽名。

translations.literal: You were first too severe; now on every matter you use leniency to buy a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: You were once too harsh; now on every issue you court favor through indulgence.

sentences.zh: 過猶不及，汝其識之！

translations.literal: Going too far is as bad as falling short—mark this well!
translations.idiomatic: Excess is no better than deficiency—remember that!

sentences.zh: 」尋請裁鹽場協辦鹽大使，改海寧草塘為石塘。

translations.literal: " Shortly thereafter he requested abolition of the salt-field assistant salt commissioners and changing Haining grass embankments to stone embankments.
translations.idiomatic: " He soon asked to abolish assistant salt commissioners at the salt fields and to convert Haining grass revetments into stone dikes.

sentences.zh: 既，又請濬備塘河運石。

translations.literal: Afterward he again requested dredging the backup embankment canal to transport stone.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also sought to dredge the backup dike canal to haul stone.

sentences.zh: 五年，上諭曰：「盧焯至浙江，沽名邀譽，舉鄉賢名宦，絡繹不絕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor instructed: "Since Lu Chao reached Zhejiang he has courted reputation, continuously recommending local worthies and famous officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year [1740] the emperor said: "Since Lu Chao reached Zhejiang he has sought fame, recommending local worthies and famous officials without pause.

sentences.zh: 海塘外已漲沙數十里，焯既請停草塘歲修，又請改建石塘。

translations.literal: Outside the seawall sand had already accreted for several tens of li; Chao had both requested stopping annual grass-embankment repairs and requested rebuilding with stone embankments.
translations.idiomatic: Sand had already built up for dozens of li beyond the seawall; Chao had both asked to halt annual grass-dike repairs and asked to rebuild in stone.

sentences.zh: 心無定見，惟事揣摩，已彰明較著矣。

translations.literal: His mind has no settled view; he only guesses at intentions—the matter is already glaringly clear.
translations.idiomatic: He has no fixed judgment and only reads the court mood—the inconsistency is plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 」六年，左都御史劉吳龍劾焯營私受賄，上解焯任，命總督德沛、副都統旺扎爾按治，事皆實，請奪官刑訊。

translations.literal: " In the sixth year Left Censor-in-Chief Liu Wulong impeached Chao for taking bribes in private interest. The emperor removed Chao from office and ordered Governor Depu and Vice Commander-in-Chief Wangzhar to investigate; the charges were all substantiated, and they requested deprivation of office and interrogation under torture.
translations.idiomatic: " In the sixth year [1741] Left Censor Liu Wulong accused Chao of private graft. The emperor dismissed him and ordered Governor Depu and Vice Commander Wangzhar to investigate; every charge proved true, and they recommended stripping his rank and putting him to the torture rack.

sentences.zh: 事連嘉湖道呂守曾、嘉興知府楊景震。

translations.literal: The case implicated Jiahu Circuit Intendant Lü Shouzeng and Jiaxing Prefect Yang Jingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The case also involved Jiahu Circuit Intendant Lü Shouzeng and Jiaxing Prefect Yang Jingzhen.

sentences.zh: 守曾已擢山西布政使，逮至浙江，自殺。

translations.literal: Shouzeng had already been promoted to Shanxi provincial treasurer; he was arrested and brought to Zhejiang, where he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzeng had already been promoted to Shanxi treasurer; seized and brought to Zhejiang, he committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 杭州民數百為焯訟冤，毀副都統廳前鼓亭。

translations.literal: Several hundred Hangzhou residents petitioned on Chao's behalf and destroyed the drum pavilion before the vice commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred Hangzhou residents pleaded Chao innocence and smashed the drum pavilion before the vice commander yamen.

sentences.zh: 德沛等以聞，上諭責辦理不妥。

translations.literal: Depu and others reported this; the emperor rebuked them for improper handling.
translations.idiomatic: Depu reported the disturbance; the emperor rebuked their handling of the affair.

sentences.zh: 七年，讞上，焯、景震皆坐不枉法贓，擬絞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the verdict was submitted; Chao and Jingzhen were both convicted of taking bribes without perverting the law and were sentenced to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year [1742] the verdict came up; Chao and Jingzhen were both found guilty of accepting bribes without twisting justice and were sentenced to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 八年，焯以完贓減等，戍軍台。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, because Chao had made restitution, his penalty was reduced by one grade and he was banished to serve at a military post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year [1743], because he had made full restitution, his sentence was reduced one grade and he was exiled to a military garrison.

sentences.zh: 十六年，上南巡，閱海塘，念焯勞，召還。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, when the emperor made a southern tour and inspected the seawall, remembering Chao's labors, he summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year [1751], during the southern tour, the emperor inspected the seawall, recalled Chao's service, and summoned him back.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授鴻臚寺少卿，署陝西西安巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and acting governor of Xi'an in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year [1755] he became Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and acting governor of Xi'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，調署湖北，以陳宏謀代焯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to act as governor of Hubei, with Chen Hongmou replacing Chao.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year [1756] he was shifted to act as governor of Hubei while Chen Hongmou was to replace him.

sentences.zh: 宏謀未至，上命發歸化城米運金川饋軍，急驛諭宏謀。

translations.literal: Hongmou had not yet arrived when the emperor ordered grain from Guihua City sent to feed the Jinchuan army and urgently dispatched a courier instruction to Hongmou.
translations.idiomatic: Before Hongmou arrived the throne ordered grain from Guihua City forwarded to supply the Jinchuan campaign and sent an urgent courier dispatch to Hongmou.

sentences.zh: 焯發視，奏言：「歸化城雖產米，路遠費重；

translations.literal: Chao inspected on dispatch and memorialized: "Though Guihua City produces grain, the route is long and the cost heavy;
translations.idiomatic: Chao inspected the order and reported: "Guihua City does produce grain, but the haul is long and costly;

sentences.zh: 西安有貯米，先發以饋軍。

translations.literal: Xi'an has stored grain—dispatch it first to feed the army.
translations.idiomatic: Xi'an holds stored grain—release that first to feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 仍請擅行罪。

translations.literal: I still request punishment for acting on my own authority.
translations.idiomatic: I still ask to be punished for acting without authorization.

sentences.zh: 」上嘉焯知大體，合機宜，實授湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised Chao for grasping the larger pattern and fitting the occasion, and formally appointed him governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised Chao for seeing the larger pattern and seizing the moment, and confirmed him as governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，西安布政使劉藻入覲，言焯在西安入貢方物，但量給薄值；

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Shaanxi provincial treasurer Liu Zao came to court and said that while Chao was in Xi'an he had presented tribute goods but only paid token prices;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year [1757] Shaanxi treasurer Liu Zao attended court and said that in Xi'an Chao had accepted tribute goods yet paid only trifling sums;

sentences.zh: 及調任湖北，欲借庫帑，未應付。

translations.literal: and that after transfer to Hubei he wished to borrow from the treasury but was refused payment.
translations.idiomatic: and that after moving to Hubei he had tried to borrow from the provincial treasury without receiving funds.

sentences.zh: 上責焯負恩，奪官，戍巴里坤。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Chao for ingratitude, stripped his office, and banished him to Barköl.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor charged Chao with ingratitude, stripped his rank, and exiled him to Barköl.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，召還。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year [1761] he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year [1767] he died.

sentences.zh: 圖爾炳阿，佟佳氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Tu Erbinga, of the Tunggiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Erbinga of the Tunggiya clan was a Manchu bannerman of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 初授吏部筆帖式，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was first appointed a clerk in the Board of Civil Appointments and was promoted through successive posts to director.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered the Board of Civil Appointments as a clerk and rose step by step to director.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，授陝西甘肅道。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he was appointed Shaanxi-Gansu Circuit Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 3 [1738] he received the Shaanxi-Gansu circuit intendantship.

sentences.zh: 累遷雲南布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted through successive posts to Yunnan provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in turn to provincial treasurer of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year [1747] he became governor.

sentences.zh: 十五年，永嘉知縣楊茂虧銀米，圖爾炳阿令後政彌補結案。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Yongjia Magistrate Yang Mao had a deficit in silver and grain; Tu Erbinga ordered his successor to make good the shortfall and closed the case.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year [1750] Yongjia Magistrate Yang Mao was short in silver and grain; Tu Erbinga told his successor to cover the deficit and closed the file.

sentences.zh: 總督碩色論劾，上責圖爾炳阿欺隱徇庇，奪官，逮京師，下刑部治罪，坐監守自盜，擬斬監候。

translations.literal: Governor Shuose impeached him in a memorial; the emperor rebuked Tu Erbinga for concealment and favoritism, stripped his office, had him arrested and brought to the capital, and handed him to the Board of Punishments, which convicted him of embezzlement while in charge and sentenced him to beheading after the autumn assizes.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Shuose memorialized against him; the emperor rebuked Tu Erbinga for covering up and showing favor, removed his rank, had him seized and brought to Beijing, and referred him to the Board of Punishments, which found embezzlement while in office and recommended beheading after the autumn assizes.

sentences.zh: 十七年，上以圖爾炳阿贓未入己，釋出獄。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, because the emperor considered that Tu Erbinga's illicit gains had not entered his own pocket, he was released from prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year [1752] the emperor held that Tu Erbinga gains had not enriched himself personally and ordered his release.

sentences.zh: 授吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed a vice director in the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director in the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授河南布政使，調山東，又復還河南。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Henan provincial treasurer, transferred to Shandong, then returned again to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Henan treasurer, was shifted to Shandong, then returned once more to Henan.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year [1755] he was promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，上南巡，江蘇布政使夏邑彭家屏以病告家居，覲徐州行在，入對，言鄉縣被水。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, during the emperor's southern tour, Jiangsu provincial treasurer Peng Jiaping of Xiayi, claiming illness, had retired home; he attended the emperor's traveling palace at Xuzhou, entered audience, and spoke of flooding in his home county.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year [1757], on the southern tour, Jiangsu treasurer Peng Jiaping of Xiayi, who had retired home on grounds of illness, came to the traveling palace at Xuzhou, was received in audience, and reported flooding in his native county.

sentences.zh: 上諮圖爾炳阿，圖爾炳阿奏收成至九分，上責圖爾炳阿文過。

translations.literal: The emperor consulted Tu Erbinga; Tu Erbinga memorialized that the harvest reached nine-tenths; the emperor rebuked Tu Erbinga for glossing over faults.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Tu Erbinga, who reported a harvest of nine-tenths; the throne rebuked him for whitewashing the facts.

sentences.zh: 圖爾炳阿又奏「去歲被水尚未成災」，上斥為怙惡不悛。

translations.literal: Tu Erbinga again memorialized that "last year's flooding has not yet become a disaster"; the emperor denounced him as incorrigible.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Erbinga memorialized again that last year floods have not yet become a disaster; the emperor called him incorrigible.

sentences.zh: 遣員外郎觀音保密察災狀得實，上奪圖爾炳阿官，髮烏里雅蘇台效力。

translations.literal: He dispatched Vice Director Guanyinbao on a secret inspection; the disaster was found real, and the emperor stripped Tu Erbinga of office and sent him to serve at Uliastai.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Vice Director Guanyinbao on a secret inspection that confirmed the disaster; Tu Erbinga was dismissed and ordered to labor at Uliastai.

sentences.zh: 上發徐州，夏邑民張欽、劉元德詣行在訴知縣孫默諱災及治賑不實，上親鞫，元德言諸生段昌緒指使。

translations.literal: When the emperor left Xuzhou, Xiayi commoners Zhang Qin and Liu Yuande came to the traveling palace to accuse Magistrate Sun Mo of concealing the disaster and mishandling relief; the emperor personally interrogated them, and Yuande said the licentiate Duan Changxu had instigated them.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Xuzhou, Xiayi residents Zhang Qin and Liu Yuande petitioned at the traveling palace that Magistrate Sun Mo had hidden the disaster and botched relief; the emperor questioned them himself, and Yuande named the licentiate Duan Changxu as instigator.

sentences.zh: 上復遣侍衛成林會圖爾炳阿至夏邑按治，於昌緒家得傳鈔吳三桂檄。

translations.literal: The emperor again dispatched Guard Cheng Lin together with Tu Erbinga to Xiayi to investigate; at Changxu's home they found a copied proclamation of Wu Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Guard Cheng Lin with Tu Erbinga to investigate in Xiayi; at Changxu's house they found a copied proclamation of Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「圖爾炳阿察出逆檄，緝邪之功大，諱災之罪小。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "Tu Erbinga uncovered the treasonous proclamation—his merit in suppressing heterodoxy is great, his offense in concealing the disaster is small.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Tu Erbinga uncovered a seditious proclamation—his merit in rooting out treason outweighs his fault in hiding the flood.

sentences.zh: 且以如此梗不知化之民，而治其司牧者以罪，是不益長澆風乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, to punish the officials who govern such stubborn, unregenerate commoners would only encourage a degenerate popular temper, would it not?
translations.idiomatic: And to punish the magistrates who rule such stubborn, unregenerate people would only feed a corrupt popular spirit, would it not?

sentences.zh: 免圖爾炳阿罪，仍留巡撫任治賑。

translations.literal: Tu Erbinga's offense is pardoned; he remains in the governorship to manage relief.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Erbinga penalty is remitted and he remains governor to oversee relief.

sentences.zh: 圖爾炳阿若因有前此罪斥之旨，心存成見，或不釋然於災民，則是自取罪戾，亦不能逃朕洞鑑。

translations.literal: If Tu Erbinga, because of the earlier order of dismissal, harbors prejudice or cannot set his heart at ease toward disaster victims, then he brings guilt on himself and cannot escape my penetrating scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: If, because of the earlier dismissal, Tu Erbinga holds a grudge or cannot treat flood victims fairly, he will invite punishment himself and cannot escape my scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 」尋家屏亦以藏禁書罪至死，圖爾炳阿仍以匿災下吏議，奪官，命留任。

translations.literal: " Shortly thereafter Jiaping was also sentenced to death for concealing banned books; Tu Erbinga was still referred to the judicial authorities for concealing disaster and was stripped of office, yet ordered to remain in post.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Jiaping was also sentenced to death for hiding banned books; Tu Erbinga was still referred for concealing the disaster, stripped of rank, yet told to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 逾數月，召詣京師，命往烏里雅蘇台治餉。

translations.literal: After several months he was summoned to the capital and ordered to go to Uliastai to manage provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was called to the capital and sent to Uliastai to manage supplies.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授貴州巡撫，二十九年，調湖南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed governor of Guizhou; in the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year [1763] he became governor of Guizhou; in the twenty-ninth [1764] he was moved to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 三十年，病作，遣醫往視。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he fell ill; the emperor sent a physician to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year [1765] he fell ill and the emperor sent a physician.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 阿思哈，薩克達氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Asiha, of the Sakda clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Asiha of the Sakda clan was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 自官學生考授內閣中書，累遷刑部郎中，充軍機處章京。

translations.literal: From student of the Imperial School he passed examination and was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat; he was promoted through successive posts to director in the Board of Punishments and served as a clerk on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: From the Imperial School he passed examination for secretary in the Grand Secretariat, rose through the Board of Punishments to director, and served as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年，擢甘肅布政使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong he was promoted to Gansu provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 10 [1745] he was promoted to Gansu treasurer.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year [1749] he became governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「各營操演槍砲，須實子彈。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In each camp, when drilling with muskets and cannon, live ammunition must be used.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Every garrison drilling with muskets and cannon must use live ammunition.

sentences.zh: 營馬應令騎兵自飼。

translations.literal: Camp horses should be fed by the cavalry themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry should feed their own mounts.

sentences.zh: 技藝以純熟得用為要，步法、架勢不必朝更夕改。

translations.literal: In martial skill, what matters is pure mastery that can be put to use; footwork and postures need not be changed morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting skill should be judged by reliable mastery, not by changing stances every day.

sentences.zh: 」上嘉其言得要。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised his words as grasping essentials.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised his advice as hitting the essentials.

sentences.zh: 旋調山西。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 十六年，平陽旱，未親往撫卹，詔責之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Pingyang suffered drought; he did not go in person to comfort and relieve, and an edict rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year [1751] Pingyang suffered drought; he did not go in person to comfort the people, and an edict rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 十七年，蒲、解等處复災，請以平陽富民捐款解河東道加賑。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Pu, Jie, and other places suffered disaster again; he requested that wealthy households in Pingyang donate funds to be forwarded through the Hedong Circuit for added relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year [1752] Pu, Jie, and other districts were stricken again; he asked wealthy men in Pingyang to donate funds to be sent through the Hedong circuit for supplemental relief.

sentences.zh: 上諭之曰：「賑濟蠲緩，重者數百萬，少亦數十萬，悉動正帑，從無顧惜。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed him: "Relief, tax remission, and deferral run from several million down to several hundred thousand—all drawn from the regular treasury without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Relief and tax remissions run from millions down to hundreds of thousands—all from the regular treasury without stint.

sentences.zh: 富戶所捐幾何，貯庫助賑，殊非體制。

translations.literal: How much can wealthy households donate? Storing it in the treasury to aid relief is quite contrary to proper practice.
translations.idiomatic: What can wealthy donors supply? Banking their gifts to aid relief violates proper practice.

sentences.zh: 此端一開，則偏災之地，貧民既苦艱食，富戶又令出貲。

translations.literal: Once this precedent is opened, in partially stricken places the poor will already suffer scarce food while the wealthy are also ordered to pay out.
translations.idiomatic: Once that door opens, in partly stricken districts the poor already lack food while the rich are pressed for cash.

sentences.zh: 國家撫卹災黎，何忍出此？

translations.literal: When the state comforts disaster victims, how can we bear to do this?
translations.idiomatic: When the state succors disaster victims, how can we impose such a burden?

sentences.zh: 」責阿思哈卑鄙錯謬，不勝巡撫任，召還，奪官。

translations.literal: " He rebuked Asiha as base and mistaken, unfit for the governorship, summoned him back, and stripped his office.
translations.idiomatic: " He called Asiha base and wrong, unfit to govern, recalled him, and stripped his rank.

sentences.zh: 尋授吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed a vice director in the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed vice director in the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 二十年，命以布政使銜往準噶爾軍前經理糧運。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was ordered to proceed to the Dzungar front with the rank of provincial treasurer to manage grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year [1755] he was sent to the Dzungar front with treasurer rank to manage grain transport.

sentences.zh: 擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，命署江西巡撫，蒞任，清理屯田，尋真除。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was ordered to act as governor of Jiangxi; on taking office he cleared up garrison fields, and shortly thereafter received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year [1757] he was ordered to act as governor of Jiangxi; on arrival he sorted out garrison fields and soon received formal appointment.

sentences.zh: 學政謝溶生劾阿思哈婪賄派累，命尚書劉統勳、侍郎常鈞等按鞫，得實，擬絞。

translations.literal: Education Commissioner Xie Rongsheng impeached Asiha for greedily taking bribes and imposing burdens; the emperor ordered Minister Liu Tongxun, Vice Minister Chang Jun, and others to investigate and interrogate; the charges were substantiated, and strangulation was recommended.
translations.idiomatic: Education Commissioner Xie Rongsheng accused Asiha of graft and extortion; the throne ordered Minister Liu Tongxun, Vice Minister Chang Jun, and others to investigate; every charge proved true, and they recommended strangulation.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，詔免罪，以三品頂戴髮烏魯木齊效力。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, an edict pardoned his offense; with a third-rank peacock feather he was sent to serve at Ürümqi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year [1761] an edict remitted his sentence; he was sent to serve at Ürümqi wearing a third-rank peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，命往伊犁協同辦事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was ordered to proceed to Ili to assist in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year [1763] he was ordered to Ili to assist in local administration.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，授廣東巡撫，調河南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed governor of Guangdong, then transferred to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year [1764] he became governor of Guangdong, then was moved to Henan.

sentences.zh: 三十年，疏言：「衛河運道淺阻，濬縣三官廟、老鸛嘴諸地砂礓挺據河心，重載尤艱浮送。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he memorialized: "The Wei River grain-transport channel is shallow and obstructed; at Sanguan Temple and Laoguanzui in Jun County and other places gravel ridges stand athwart the river center, making heavily laden transport especially difficult to float through.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year [1765] he reported: "The Wei River grain route runs shallow and blocked; at Sanguan Temple, Laoguanzui, and other spots in Jun County, gravel ridges jut into mid-channel, and heavily laden boats can barely be floated through.

sentences.zh: 向於上、下游淺處建築草壩以束水勢。

translations.literal: Previously grass dams were built at shallow points upstream and downstream to confine the water's force.
translations.idiomatic: Grass dams had been built at shallow reaches upstream and downstream to concentrate the current.

sentences.zh: 詳考河形，夏秋水盛，無須草壩；

translations.literal: On detailed examination of the river's form, in summer and autumn when the water is full, grass dams are unnecessary;
translations.idiomatic: A close study of the channel shows that in summer and autumn, when the water runs high, grass dams serve no purpose;

sentences.zh: 冬令源澀，草壩亦屬無益。

translations.literal: in winter when the sources run low, grass dams are likewise of no use.
translations.idiomatic: in winter, when the sources run low, they are equally useless.

sentences.zh: 不如於上游先期蓄水，臨時開放。

translations.literal: It would be better to store water upstream in advance and release it when needed.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to impound water upstream beforehand and release it when required.

sentences.zh: 飭府縣督河員於九月望後起，至漕船出境止，暫閉外河以上民渠，使水歸官渠，重運自可疏通。

translations.literal: Order prefectures, counties, and river officials to begin after the fifteenth of the ninth month and continue until the grain boats depart the region, temporarily closing civilian canals above the outer channel so water returns to the official channel, and heavy transport can then be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures, counties, and river officers should begin after the mid-ninth month and continue until the grain fleet has passed, temporarily shutting civilian canals above the outer channel so the water gathers in the official channel and heavy transport can move freely.

sentences.zh: 鑿去砂礓，並集夫疏濬浮沙，以利漕運。

translations.literal: Chisel away the gravel ridges and assemble laborers to dredge floating sand to benefit grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: The gravel ridges should be cut away and labor assembled to dredge drifting sand and ease grain transport.

sentences.zh: 」又請借司庫閒款，委員分購河工料物，以除沿河州縣按畝派累，均報聞。

translations.literal: " He also requested borrowing idle funds from the provincial treasury, commissioning officers to purchase river-work materials in bulk, to eliminate the practice of apportioning burdens on households along the river by the mu, and all was reported and approved.
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked to borrow idle treasury funds and send officers to buy river materials in bulk, ending the practice of levying burdens on riparian counties by the mu; all was reported and approved.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，擢雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year [1769] he was elevated to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 師徵緬甸，阿思哈出銅壁關至蠻暮軍中，奏軍中糧馬不敷。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against Burma, Asiha went from Tongbi Pass to Manmu in the army camp and memorialized that grain and horses in the army were insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: During the Burma campaign Asiha went from Tongbi Pass to the camp at Manmu and reported that army grain and horses were inadequate.

sentences.zh: 上責其畏難，解任，以副都統銜在領隊大臣上行走。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for fearing difficulties, removed him from office, and ordered him to serve with vice commander-in-chief rank above the expedition commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him for shrinking from hardship, dismissed him, and ordered him to serve with vice commander rank above the expedition commanders.

sentences.zh: 旋召為吏部侍郎，入對失上指，奪官，戍伊犁。

translations.literal: He was soon recalled as vice minister of the Board of Civil Appointments; his audience failed to please the emperor, his office was stripped, and he was banished to serve at Ili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as vice minister of the Board of Civil Appointments, but his audience displeased the emperor; his rank was stripped and he was exiled to Ili.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，釋回，仍充軍機章京。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was released and returned, and again served as a Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year [1774] he was released and again served as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 擢左都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 大學士舒赫德師討王倫，命阿思哈偕額駙拉旺多爾濟率健銳、火器兩營以往。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shuhede commanded troops to suppress Wang Lun; Asiha was ordered to proceed together with Imperial Son-in-Law Lawangduoerji leading the Vanguard and Firearms camps.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shuhede led troops against Wang Lun; Asiha was ordered to go with Imperial Son-in-Law Lawangduoerji at the head of the Vanguard and Firearms camps.

sentences.zh: 事定，拉旺多爾濟言城北搜剿王倫餘黨，阿思哈未同往，下吏議，奪官，命留任。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Lawangduoerji reported searching north of the city to wipe out Wang Lun's remaining followers, but Asiha had not gone with him; he was referred to the judicial authorities, stripped of office, yet ordered to remain in post.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, Lawangduoerji reported a sweep north of the city for Wang Lun's remnants, but Asiha had not accompanied him; he was referred for judgment, stripped of rank, yet told to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，署吏部尚書，旋授漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he acted as minister of the Board of Civil Appointments, then was appointed Grain Transport Governor-General.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year [1776] he acted as minister of the Board of Civil Appointments, then became Grain Transport Governor-General.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜祭葬，諡莊恪。

translations.literal: He died; funeral sacrifices and burial honors were granted, and he was posthumously titled Zhuangke.
translations.idiomatic: He died; the court granted funeral sacrifices and burial honors and gave him the posthumous title Zhuangke.

sentences.zh: 阿思哈初撫江西，上眷之獨厚。

translations.literal: When Asiha first governed Jiangxi, the emperor's favor toward him alone was especially thick.
translations.idiomatic: When Asiha first governed Jiangxi, the emperor's favor toward him was unusually deep.

sentences.zh: 廣西巡撫衛哲治入覲，上問各省督撫孰為最劣，哲治引罪，上謂：「姑置汝！

translations.literal: Guangxi Governor Wei Zhezhi came to court; the emperor asked which provincial governors and governors-general were the worst; Zhezhi took blame upon himself, and the emperor said: "For the present, set you aside!
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi Governor Wei Zhezhi attended court; the emperor asked which governors and governors-general were worst; Zhezhi took the blame on himself, and the emperor said, "For now, I shall set you aside!

sentences.zh: 」哲治舉阿思哈對，時以為難能。

translations.literal: " Zhezhi named Asiha in reply; at the time this was considered hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhezhi named Asiha instead; at the time people thought that took uncommon courage.

sentences.zh: 宮兆麟，字伯厚，江南懷遠人。

translations.literal: Gong Zhaolin, style name Bohou, was a native of Huaiyuan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhaolin, whose style was Bohou, came from Huaiyuan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 自貢生授湖北安陸通判，累遷至山東糧道。

translations.literal: From tribute student he was appointed subprefectural judge of Anlu in Hubei and was promoted through successive posts to Shandong Grain Transport Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: As a tribute student he received appointment as subprefectural judge of Anlu in Hubei and rose step by step to Shandong Grain Transport Intendant.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年，授湖南按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong he was appointed Hunan provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 31 [1766] he became Hunan provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 桂陽州民侯七郎毆殺從兄岳添，賄其兄學添自承。

translations.literal: Guiyang Prefecture commoner Hou Qilang beat and killed his cousin's servant Yue Tian; he bribed his elder cousin Xue Tian to confess on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Qilang, a commoner of Guiyang Prefecture, beat and killed his cousin's servant Yue Tian and bribed his elder cousin Xue Tian to confess in his place.

sentences.zh: 知州張宏燧讞上，巡撫李因培疑之，令兆麟詳鞫得實。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhang Hongsui submitted the verdict; Governor Li Yinpei was suspicious and had Zhaolin conduct a detailed interrogation, obtaining the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Hongsui sent up the verdict; Governor Li Yinpei was doubtful and had Zhaolin re-examine the case until the facts emerged.

sentences.zh: 因培調福建去，巡撫常鈞庇宏燧，以七郎呼冤劾兆麟，兆麟亦入奏。

translations.literal: Yinpei was transferred to Fujian; Governor Chang Jun shielded Hongsui; Qilang petitioned for justice and impeached Zhaolin, and Zhaolin also memorialized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yinpei was transferred to Fujian; Governor Chang Jun protected Hongsui; Qilang cried injustice and impeached Zhaolin, and Zhaolin memorialized the throne in turn.

sentences.zh: 上遣侍郎期成額會總督定長按治，如兆麟讞；

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched Vice Minister Qicheng'e together with Governor Ding Chang to investigate; the verdict agreed with Zhaolin's;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Minister Qicheng'e with Governor Ding Chang to investigate; the findings matched Zhaolin's verdict;

sentences.zh: 兆麟又發宏燧買金行賄狀，期成額等奏聞，逮訊，買金非行賄，乃迎合因培及湖北布政使赫升額意指，代武陵知縣馮其柘補虧空。

translations.literal: Zhaolin further exposed Hongsui's buying gold to pay bribes; Qicheng'e and others memorialized; on arrest and interrogation, the gold purchase was not for bribery but to accommodate Yinpei and Hubei provincial treasurer He Sheng'e's intent, covering the deficit for Wuling Magistrate Feng Qituo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin further exposed Hongsui's purchase of gold as bribery; Qicheng'e and others reported it; on arrest and questioning, the gold proved not a bribe but a move to accommodate Yinpei and Hubei treasurer He Sheng'e by covering Wuling Magistrate Feng Qituo's deficit.

sentences.zh: 因培、赫升額、常鈞、宏燧皆坐譴。

translations.literal: Yinpei, He Sheng'e, Chang Jun, and Hongsui were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: Yinpei, He Sheng'e, Chang Jun, and Hongsui were all censured.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，兆麟調雲南按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year Zhaolin was transferred to Yunnan judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year [1767] Zhaolin was transferred to Yunnan judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，遷布政使，擢廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was moved to provincial treasurer and promoted to Guangxi governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year [1768] he became provincial treasurer and was elevated to governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 雲南軍營需硝，敕兆麟籌畫，兆麟以廣西舊存硝七萬七千餘斤運剝隘，复撥通省營貯火藥二十萬斤繼運，得旨嘉許。

translations.literal: Yunnan army camps needed saltpeter; the emperor ordered Zhaolin to plan it; Zhaolin transported more than seventy-seven thousand jin of saltpeter formerly stored in Guangxi to Bodun Pass, and also allocated two hundred thousand jin of gunpowder stored province-wide in camps for continued transport; the edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan camps needed saltpeter; the emperor ordered Zhaolin to arrange supplies; he shipped more than seventy-seven thousand jin of saltpeter stored in Guangxi to Bodun Pass and then forwarded two hundred thousand jin of gunpowder from camps across the province; the throne commended him.

sentences.zh: 調湖南。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，又調貴州。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he was again transferred to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year [1770] he was moved again to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 桐梓縣民為亂，命速赴任，會湖廣總督吳達善捕治。

translations.literal: Tongzi County commoners rebelled; he was ordered to hasten to his post; coincidentally Huguang Governor-General Wu Dashan captured and punished them.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners in Tongzi County rose in revolt; he was ordered to hurry to his post, where Huguang Governor-General Wu Dashan was already capturing and punishing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 亂定，古州黨堆寨苗香要等為亂，复偕吳達善督兵捕誅之。

translations.literal: When the disorder was settled, Miao Xiangyao and others of Dangduizhai in Guzhou rebelled; he again joined Wu Dashan in supervising troops to capture and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: After that disturbance was settled, the Miao Xiangyao and others of Dangduizhai in Guzhou rebelled; he again joined Wu Dashan in leading troops to capture and execute them.

sentences.zh: 兆麟奏黨堆寨苗老呴以阻香要亂被殺，令即寨立廟以祀良苗，並將死義被旌及香要叛逆伏誅狀，譯苗語榜廟門，俾令警戒；

translations.literal: Zhaolin memorialized that the Miao elder Lao Xu at Dangduizhai was killed for blocking Xiangyao's rebellion and requested a temple be built at the stockade to worship worthy Miao; also translating into Miao language on the temple gate the list of those who died loyal and were commended and Xiangyao's rebellion and execution for warning;
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin reported that the Miao elder Lao Xu of Dangduizhai had been killed for resisting Xiangyao's rebellion and asked that a temple be built at the stockade to honor worthy Miao; he also had posted at the gate, in Miao translation, an account of the loyal dead who had been commended and of Xiangyao's rebellion and execution as a warning;

sentences.zh: 並請移駐將吏，建下江營土城，駐兵鎮撫。

translations.literal: he also requested transferring stationed officers and soldiers, building an earthen walled camp at Xiajiang to station troops for pacification.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked to relocate stationed officers and soldiers, build an earthen walled camp at Xiajiang, and post troops to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 是夏，兆麟奏請於鄰省湖南、四川、廣西買米運貴州糶濟。

translations.literal: That summer Zhaolin memorialized requesting purchase of grain in neighboring provinces Hunan, Sichuan, and Guangxi to transport to Guizhou for famine-relief sale.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Zhaolin asked to buy grain in neighboring Hunan, Sichuan, and Guangxi and ship it to Guizhou for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 至秋，豐收，復奏請停運。

translations.literal: By autumn the harvest was abundant; he again memorialized to stop transport.
translations.idiomatic: By autumn the harvest was abundant, and he memorialized again to halt the shipments.

sentences.zh: 上斥其冒昧，勗令詳慎。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for rashness and exhorted him to be detailed and careful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called him rash and urged him to be thorough and cautious.

sentences.zh: 兆麟復奏請簡發知府三員赴貴州，上以「此端一開，各省效尤，妨吏部選法；

translations.literal: Zhaolin again memorialized requesting dispatch of three prefects to Guizhou; the emperor said: "Once this precedent is opened, every province will follow suit, obstructing the Board's selection methods;
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin memorialized again asking that three prefects be sent to Guizhou; the emperor replied, "Once that door opens, every province will follow suit and obstruct the Board of Civil Appointments' selection rules;

sentences.zh: 且開幸進之門」，下旨嚴飭。

translations.literal: and it opens a door to opportunistic advancement," and issued a stern edict.
translations.idiomatic: and it opens a path for opportunists to advance," and issued a stern rebuke.

sentences.zh: 會貴州布政使觀音保入覲，訐兆麟粗率喜自誇，口給便捷，人號為「鐵嘴」。

translations.literal: When Guizhou provincial treasurer Guanyinbao came to court he denounced Zhaolin as crude, fond of self-praise, glib and quick-witted; people called him "Iron Mouth."
translations.idiomatic: When Guizhou treasurer Guanyinbao attended court he accused Zhaolin of being crude, boastful, and glib; people called Zhaolin "Iron Mouth."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「觀音保人已粗率，今尚以兆麟為粗率，則粗率更甚可知。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Guanyinbao himself is crude; if he still calls Zhaolin crude, then Zhaolin's crudeness must be still more evident.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Guanyinbao is crude himself; if he still finds Zhaolin crude, Zhaolin must be cruder still.

sentences.zh: 」諭兆麟猛省痛改。

translations.literal: " He instructed Zhaolin to reflect deeply and reform painfully.
translations.idiomatic: " He told Zhaolin to reflect deeply and reform at once.

sentences.zh: 尋詔詣京師，降補甘肅按察使。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was summoned to the capital and demoted to Gansu judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned to the capital and demoted to Gansu judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，坐貴州任內失察廠員虧欠鉛斤，奪官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, for failing to supervise while in Guizhou office, allowing factory officials' deficit in lead weight, his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year [1771] he was stripped of rank for failing, while governing Guizhou, to detect factory officials' deficit in lead.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，東巡，兆麟迎駕，詔與三品銜。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, on the eastern tour, Zhaolin greeted the imperial procession; an edict granted third-rank peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year [1776], during the eastern tour, Zhaolin greeted the imperial procession and received a third-rank peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year [1781] he died.

sentences.zh: 楊景素，字樸園，江南甘泉人，提督捷孫。

translations.literal: Yang Jingsu, style name Puyuan, was a native of Ganquan in Jiangnan, grandson of Regional Commander Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jingsu, whose style was Puyuan, came from Ganquan in Jiangnan and was grandson of Regional Commander Jie.

sentences.zh: 父鑄，古北口總兵。

translations.literal: His father Zhu was regional commander at Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhu had been regional commander at Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 景素孱弱，不好章句，貧不能自給。

translations.literal: Jingsu was frail and weak, disliked literary composition, and in poverty could not support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu was frail, cared little for classical learning, and was too poor to support himself.

sentences.zh: 入貲授縣丞，發直隸河工效力。

translations.literal: He purchased office and was appointed county subprefect, then sent to Zhili to serve on river works.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased office and received appointment as county subprefect, then was sent to Zhili to serve on river works.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，補蠡縣縣丞，累遷保定知府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he was appointed county subprefect of Lixian and was promoted through successive posts to prefect of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 3 [1738] he became county subprefect of Lixian and rose step by step to prefect of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授福建汀漳龍道。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed Tingzhanglong Circuit Intendant in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year [1753] he received the Tingzhanglong circuit intendantship in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 漳浦民蔡榮祖欲為亂，景素率營卒擒斬之。

translations.literal: Zhangpu commoner Cai Rongzu intended rebellion; Jingsu led camp soldiers to capture and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Rongzu, a commoner of Zhangpu, plotted rebellion; Jingsu led camp soldiers to seize and behead him.

sentences.zh: 調台灣道。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Taiwan Circuit Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Taiwan circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 釐定漢民墾種地，並生熟番界址。

translations.literal: He defined boundaries for Han civilian reclaimed land and between raw and acculturated aborigines.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed boundaries for Han reclaimed land and between raw and acculturated aborigine territories.

sentences.zh: 革遊民為通譯而不法者，代以熟番。

translations.literal: He eliminated vagrants serving as interpreters who acted unlawfully and replaced them with acculturated aborigines.
translations.idiomatic: He removed vagrant interpreters who abused their office and replaced them with acculturated aborigines.

sentences.zh: 又禁入山採木，借修造戰船材料為名，累諸番。

translations.literal: He also prohibited entering the mountains to cut timber, using repair materials for warships as a pretext, which burdened the various aborigines.
translations.idiomatic: He also forbade timber cutting in the mountains on the pretext of supplying warship repairs, a burden that fell on the aborigines.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，授河南按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was appointed Henan provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year [1768] he became Henan provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，擢甘肅布政使，調直隸。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he was promoted to Gansu provincial treasurer, then transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year [1770] he was promoted to Gansu treasurer, then moved to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 命從尚書裘曰修勘察堤埝各工。

translations.literal: He was ordered to follow Minister Qiu Yuexiu in inspecting dikes and embankment works.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to accompany Minister Qiu Yuexiu in inspecting dikes and embankment works.

sentences.zh: 坐失察雄縣知縣胡錫瑛侵蝕災賑，下吏議，奪官，命留任，俟八年無過，方准開復。

translations.literal: For failing to supervise Xiongxian Magistrate Hu Xiying's embezzlement of disaster relief, he was referred to the judicial authorities, stripped of office, yet ordered to remain in post; only after eight years without offense could rehabilitation be approved.
translations.idiomatic: For failing to detect Xiongxian Magistrate Hu Xiying's embezzlement of disaster relief funds, he was referred for judgment, stripped of rank, yet told to remain in office; rehabilitation would be allowed only after eight years without fault.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，壽張民王倫為亂，大學士舒赫德督兵討之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year Shouzhang commoner Wang Lun rebelled; Grand Secretary Shuhede commanded troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year [1774] Wang Lun, a commoner of Shouzhang, rebelled; Grand Secretary Shuhede led troops to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 上命景素具車馬濟師，令分守河西。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jingsu to supply carts and horses to aid the army and to divide command guarding the west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jingsu to furnish carts and horses for the army and to hold the west bank of the river.

sentences.zh: 賊以糧艘結浮橋欲渡，景素與總兵萬朝興、副將瑪爾當阿等督兵御之，董勸回民助師。

translations.literal: The rebels used grain boats to form a pontoon bridge intending to cross; Jingsu with Regional Commander Wan Chaoxing, Vice Commander Mardang'a, and others supervised troops to resist, urging Hui Muslims to assist the army.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels lashed grain boats into a pontoon bridge to cross; Jingsu, with Regional Commander Wan Chaoxing, Vice Commander Mardang'a, and others, led troops to block them and urged Hui communities to aid the army.

sentences.zh: 夜焚橋，賊不得渡。

translations.literal: At night they burned the bridge; the rebels could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: They burned the bridge by night, and the rebels could not cross.

sentences.zh: 事旋定，擢山東巡撫。

translations.literal: When the affair was soon settled he was promoted to Shandong governor.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was soon crushed he was promoted to governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 疏請編查保甲。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting compilation and inspection of the baojia system.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking to compile and inspect the baojia household registers.

sentences.zh: 四十年，疏請選京師健銳、火器營裨佐發山東，司營伍教演。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he memorialized requesting selection of adjutants from Beijing Vanguard and Firearms camps to dispatch to Shandong to oversee camps and drill troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year [1775] he asked that adjutants be chosen from the Beijing Vanguard and Firearms camps and sent to Shandong to oversee garrisons and drill troops.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，上東巡，臨視臨清毀橋斷道及亂民竄據所在，景素述當時戰狀，上嘉其勞，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year on the eastern tour the emperor personally inspected the destroyed bridge and cut roads at Linqing and where rebels had fled; Jingsu described the battle at the time; the emperor praised his labors and granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year [1776], on the eastern tour, the emperor inspected the ruined bridge and severed roads at Linqing and the places rebels had held; Jingsu described the fighting; the emperor praised his service and granted a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 汶上宋家窪舊渠淤墊，瀦水淹民田。

translations.literal: At Songjiawa in Wenshang an old channel was silted and blocked; stored water flooded civilian fields.
translations.idiomatic: At Songjiawa in Wenshang an old channel had silted up, and backed-up water flooded civilian fields.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，景素奏請濬舊渠，並開支河二，令仍趨南陽、昭陽二湖，下部議行。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year Jingsu memorialized requesting dredging the old channel and opening two branch channels so water again flowed to Nanyang and Zhaoyang lakes; the ministry deliberated and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year [1777] Jingsu asked to dredge the old channel and open two branch canals so the water would again reach Nanyang and Zhaoyang lakes; the ministry approved and carried it out.

sentences.zh: 擢兩廣總督，四十三年，調閩浙。

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi; in the forty-third year he was transferred to Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi; in the forty-third year [1778] he was moved to Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「浙西歉收，總督楊廷璋請撥台灣倉穀十萬接濟。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Western Zhejiang had poor harvest; Governor-General Yang Tingzhang requested allocation of one hundred thousand shi of Taiwan granary grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Western Zhejiang had a poor harvest; Governor-General Yang Tingzhang asked to allocate one hundred thousand shi of Taiwan granary grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 北風盛發，未能即到。

translations.literal: North winds were strong; it could not arrive promptly.
translations.idiomatic: Strong north winds were blowing, and the grain could not arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 請於福州、福寧、興化、泉州四府屬撥倉穀十萬，聽商運赴嘉、湖出糶；

translations.literal: Request allocation of one hundred thousand shi from granaries in Fuzhou, Funing, Xinghua, and Quanzhou prefectures under jurisdiction, allowing merchants to transport for sale in Jia and Hu;
translations.idiomatic: He asked to release one hundred thousand shi from granaries in the jurisdictions of Fuzhou, Funing, Xinghua, and Quanzhou and let merchants ship it to Jiaxing and Huzhou for sale;

sentences.zh: 仍飭台灣運歸四府補倉。

translations.literal: still order Taiwan grain transported back to replenish the four prefectures' granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan grain would still be shipped back to refill the four prefectures' granaries.

sentences.zh: 」得旨嘉獎。

translations.literal: " The edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne commended the plan.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，調直隸。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was transferred to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year [1779] he was transferred to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 薦於易簡為布政使，上以易簡為大學士敏中弟，責景素。

translations.literal: He recommended Yu Jian as provincial treasurer; the emperor said Yu Jian was younger brother of Grand Secretary Minzhong, and rebuked Jingsu.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Yu Jian for provincial treasurer; the emperor noted that Yu Jian was the younger brother of Grand Secretary Minzhong and rebuked Jingsu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，卒，贈太子太保，賜卹如例。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died; posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; mourning gifts according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he died; the court posthumously granted him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and mourning gifts according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，兩廣總督巴延三奏景素操守不謹，並發官兵得贓縱盜狀。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year Guangdong-Guangxi Governor-General Bayansan memorialized that Jingsu's integrity was not strict, also exposing troops receiving bribes and releasing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year [1780] Guangdong-Guangxi Governor-General Bayansan reported that Jingsu's conduct had not been strict and also exposed troops who took bribes and released bandits.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督薩載勘有河堤城垣工程，罰景素家屬承修。

translations.literal: Liangjiang Governor-General Sa Zai investigated river dikes and city wall works and fined Jingsu's family to undertake repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liangjiang Governor-General Sa Zai found river-dike and city-wall projects outstanding and ordered Jingsu's family to complete the repairs at their own expense.

sentences.zh: 福康安又奏景素在兩廣婪索商捐六萬餘，責景素子炤限年繳還。

translations.literal: Fuk'anggan again memorialized that Jingsu in Guangdong and Guangxi extorted over sixty thousand from merchants' donations; ordered Jingsu's son Zhao to repay within a limited term.
translations.idiomatic: Fuk'anggan also reported that in Guangdong and Guangxi Jingsu had extorted more than sixty thousand in merchant levies and ordered his son Zhao to repay within a set term.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，以福建吏治廢弛，追咎景素，戍召伊犁。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, because Fujian officialdom was lax, Jingsu was held retrospectively accountable and banished to serve at Yili.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year [1789], because Fujian governance had grown lax, Jingsu was held retrospectively accountable and banished to serve at Yili.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，釋回。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year [1794] he was released and returned home.

sentences.zh: 閔鶚元，字少儀，浙江歸安人。

translations.literal: Min Eyuan, style name Shaoyi, was a native of Gui'an in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Min Eyuan, whose style was Shaoyi, came from Gui'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a secretary in the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 10 [1745] he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a secretary in the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中，督山東學政。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to director and supervised Shandong education.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to director and supervised education in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，自學政授山東按察使，調安徽。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, from education commissioner he was appointed Shandong judicial commissioner, then transferred to Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year [1762] he moved from education commissioner to Shandong judicial commissioner, then to Anhui.

sentences.zh: 遷湖北布政使，調廣西、江寧。

translations.literal: He was moved to Hubei provincial treasurer, then transferred to Guangxi and Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He became Hubei provincial treasurer, then served in Guangxi and Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，遷安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was transferred to Anhui governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year [1776] he was transferred to governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，雲貴總督李侍堯以贓敗，罪至斬，下大學士、九卿議，請從重立決；

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year Yunnan-Guizhou Governor Li Shiyao was ruined by bribery; his crime reached decapitation; the case was referred to the Grand Secretaries and Nine Ministers for deliberation, who requested immediate execution with aggravated severity;
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year [1779] Yunnan-Guizhou Governor Li Shiyao fell to bribery; the penalty reached decapitation; the Grand Secretaries and Nine Ministers recommended immediate execution with aggravated severity;

sentences.zh: 復下各省督撫議，咸請如大學士九卿議。

translations.literal: It was again referred to the governors-general and governors of the provinces for deliberation; all requested accordance with the Grand Secretaries and Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The case was sent again to provincial governors; all endorsed the capital recommendation.

sentences.zh: 鶚元窺上指欲寬侍堯，獨奏言：「侍堯歷任封疆，勤幹有為，中外推服。

translations.literal: Eyuan divined that the emperor wished to be lenient toward Shiyao and memorialized alone: "Shiyao has served on the frontiers, been diligent and capable, and is respected within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Eyuan sensed the emperor wished to spare Shiyao and memorialized alone: "Shiyao has held frontier posts, worked diligently, and won respect at court and abroad.

sentences.zh: 請用議勤、議能例，稍寬一線。

translations.literal: I request application of the precedents for deliberating on diligence and on ability, granting slight leniency.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the precedents weighing diligence and ability be applied to grant him a measure of mercy.

sentences.zh: 」上從之，侍堯得復起。

translations.literal: " The emperor assented; Shiyao was able to rise again.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed, and Shiyao was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，調江蘇。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was transferred to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year [1780] he was transferred to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，甘肅布政使王亶望坐偽災冒賑得罪，事連鶚元弟同知鵷元。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year Gansu provincial treasurer Wang Tanwang was convicted for fabricating disaster and fraudulently drawing relief; the case implicated Eyuan's younger brother, Subprefect Yuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year [1781] Gansu treasurer Wang Tanwang was punished for inventing disasters and embezzling relief funds; the case also involved Eyuan's brother, subprefect Yuanyuan.

sentences.zh: 上責鶚元隱忍瞻徇，知其事而不舉，降三品頂戴，停廉俸。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Eyuan for concealing and showing favoritism, knowing the matter yet not reporting it; his hat knob was reduced to third rank and his integrity stipend suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor charged Eyuan with concealment and favoritism for knowing the affair yet failing to report it; his rank insignia was cut to third grade and his integrity stipend halted.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，還原品頂戴，支廉俸如故。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year his original rank insignia was restored and his integrity stipend paid as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year [1783] his original rank insignia and integrity stipend were restored.

sentences.zh: 五十年，江南旱。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year Jiangnan suffered drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year [1785] Jiangnan suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 五月，鶚元奏淮、徐、海三府如得雨二三寸，猶可種雜糧。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Eyuan memorialized that in the Huai, Xu, and Hai prefectures, if two or three inches of rain fell, miscellaneous grains could still be planted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Eyuan reported that Huai, Xu, and Hai prefectures could still plant secondary grains if they received two or three inches of rain.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「得雨二三寸未為霑足，焉能種雜糧？

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "Two or three inches of rain does not constitute adequate soaking—how can miscellaneous grains be planted?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Two or three inches of rain is not enough to soak the fields—how can secondary grains be planted?

sentences.zh: 地方雨水，民瘼攸關。

translations.literal: Local rainfall bears directly on the people's suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Rainfall in each district is bound up with the people's welfare.

sentences.zh: 鶚元何得含混入告？

translations.literal: How can Eyuan mix truth and falsehood in his reports?
translations.idiomatic: How can Eyuan blur fact and fiction in his reports?

sentences.zh: 」尋奏請截漕十萬石，淮、徐、海三府州被災較重，碾米治賑，如所議行。

translations.literal: " Shortly thereafter he memorialized to divert one hundred thousand shi of tribute grain; the Huai, Xu, and Hai prefectures and departments had suffered more heavily, and husked rice was to be distributed for relief, as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: " He soon asked to divert one hundred thousand shi of tribute grain; Huai, Xu, and Hai had suffered worst, and husked rice was to be issued for relief as he proposed.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，高郵巡檢陳倚道察知書吏偽印重徵，知州吳瑍置不問；

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year Gaoyou Subinspector Chen Yidao discovered that clerks had forged seals to levy extra taxes; Prefect Wu Yin ignored it;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year [1790] Gaoyou subinspector Chen Yidao found clerks forging seals to over-collect taxes; Prefect Wu Yin took no action;

sentences.zh: 牒上，鶚元亦置不問，揭報戶部。

translations.literal: when the report was forwarded upward, Eyuan also ignored it and merely forwarded notice to the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: when the report reached him Eyuan also ignored it and merely notified the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 上諮鶚元，鶚元猶庇瑍不以實陳，乃遣尚書慶桂、侍郎王昶按治；

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Eyuan; Eyuan still shielded Yin and did not report truthfully, so Ministers Qinggui and Vice Minister Wang Chang were dispatched to investigate;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Eyuan, who still shielded Yin and withheld the facts; Ministers Qinggui and Vice Minister Wang Chang were sent to investigate;

sentences.zh: 責鶚元欺罔，奪官，逮鶚元等下刑部治罪。

translations.literal: Eyuan was rebuked for deception, stripped of office, and Eyuan and others were arrested and handed to the Board of Punishments for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Eyuan was charged with deception, dismissed, and he and others were arrested and referred to the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 巡撫福崧劾鶚元得句容知縣王光陛牒發糧書侵挪錢糧，但令江寧府察覈。

translations.literal: Governor Fusong impeached Eyuan for receiving a memorial from Jurong Magistrate Wang Guangbi exposing grain clerks' embezzlement of funds and grain, yet only ordering Jiangning Prefecture to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Fusong accused Eyuan of receiving Jurong Magistrate Wang Guangbi report on grain clerks embezzling funds yet only telling Jiangning Prefecture to look into it.

sentences.zh: 上責鶚元玩視民瘼，徇情骫法，命置重典。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Eyuan for treating the people's suffering lightly and bending the law through favoritism, ordering severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor charged Eyuan with neglecting the people's plight and twisting the law through favoritism, and ordered the heaviest penalty.

sentences.zh: 獄具，擬斬立決，命改監候。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, immediate decapitation was recommended; the emperor ordered it changed to imprisonment awaiting execution after the autumn assizes.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict recommended immediate decapitation; the emperor commuted it to imprisonment awaiting the autumn assizes.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，釋還裡。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he was released and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year [1791] he was released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 2 [1797] he died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：法者所以持天下之平。

translations.literal: Commentary: Law exists to uphold fairness throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Law exists to uphold fairness under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 人君馭群臣，既知其不肖，乃以一日之愛憎喜怒，屈法以從之，此非細故也。

translations.literal: When a ruler governs his ministers, knowing they are unworthy yet bending the law to suit a day's love, hate, joy, or anger—this is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler knows his ministers are unworthy yet bends the law to a day's whim of favor or anger, that is no trifling lapse.

sentences.zh: 焯、阿思哈、景素坐貪皆勘實，猶尚復起；

translations.literal: Chao, Asiha, and Jingsu were all convicted of greed with substantiated findings, yet were still restored;
translations.idiomatic: Chao, Asiha, and Jingsu were all proved guilty of graft, yet were brought back;

sentences.zh: 圖爾炳阿匿災至面謾，反誅告者；

translations.literal: Tu Erbinga concealed disaster to the point of brazen deceit, yet punished those who reported it;
translations.idiomatic: Tu Erbinga hid disasters until he lied to the emperor's face, yet punished the petitioners;

sentences.zh: 兆麟口給，鶚元迎上指，至不勝疆政而始去之。

translations.literal: Zhaolin was glib; Eyuan courted the emperor's intent—only when they could no longer bear frontier governance were they removed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolin was all talk; Eyuan read the emperor's mood—only when they proved unfit for frontier rule were they finally dismissed.

sentences.zh: 高宗常謂：「朕非甚懦弱姑息之主，不能執法。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor often said: "I am not a very weak, indulgent ruler who cannot enforce the law.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qianlong often said: "I am no weak, indulgent sovereign who cannot enforce the law.

sentences.zh: 」執法固難，自克其愛憎喜怒，尤不易言也。

translations.literal: " Enforcing the law is indeed difficult; mastering one's own loves, hates, joys, and angers is even harder to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: " Enforcing the law is hard enough; mastering one's own passions is harder still.
